change: Layout 1 (pre-launch, changed in place): containers that more than one replica can create — below the nearest row or the document, under an optional field or a record entry — are Loro mergeable containers (ensure_mergeable_*); others stay regular. Removing a value, a row holding one, or undoing either first empties the mergeable containers inside; creating one empties it before filling. Setting a present object reconciles field by field.
why: Concurrent first creation of the same optional value or record entry made two containers and hid one. Loro retains mergeable containers by identity, including in shallow snapshots, so removal must empty them.

workloads.rowChurn: 50 rounds of inserting and removing 20 rows, each with ~1 KB text, a 10-string list and an optional object holding ~1 KB text
workloads.recordChurn: 50 rounds of setting and clearing 20 record entries under keys never reused, each an object with ~1 KB text

churnCost.note: trimmedBytes is a shallow snapshot at the latest version; untouchedBytes is a fresh document with the same final value.

withoutRelease.note: Probe with row release disabled: removed rows kept their optional object's text.

churnCost.reading: Each mergeable container ever created stays, empty, at about 19 bytes (one per optional text, two per optional object holding text). Regular row children are still reclaimed. Record churn already kept ~9 bytes per removed key as map tombstones.

coreCost.note: Two runs each side. 1000-row metrics agree within noise; 5000-row metrics vary 20-40% between runs on both sides. The checklist fixture holds no mergeable containers.
